transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-28
Start time: 16:30 UTC
Duration: 78 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Dr. Lena Morales (CISO, Novus), Ari Chen (Head of Infrastructure, Novus), Samir Patel (Platform Eng., Novus), Maya Ito (Compliance)

Summary:
Quick but deep technical walk through of Novus's private deployment constraints: strict data residency, SOC 2+ISO plans, enforced SSO with SAML, RBAC zones, no public internet egress for model data, and requirement for KMS integration and audit log forwarding. Focus on network isolation, egress gateways, split-horizon DNS, and firewall rule templates.

Topics covered:
- Deployment modes (private VPC vs air-gapped on-prem)
- Ingress patterns (API proxies, mutual TLS)
- Egress control (allow-listing egress endpoints, outbound gateways)
- KMS integration and key rotation workflows
- Audit logs and SIEM integration (log retention, PII redaction)
- RBAC and SSO mapping for SAML groups and service accounts

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll run through our architecture suggestions and make sure we capture any constraints. Priya will lead the infra bits, I'll handle procurement/next steps.
[00:22] Priya (Redwood SE): Hi all, quick agenda: network isolation, ingress/egress, key management, and logging. We also want to surface failure modes and fallback — e.g., if Dedicated pool hits capacity what happens to requests?
[00:45] Dr. Lena: Great, thanks. Our main thing is we cannot allow model input to leave EU residency unless it's encrypted with customer-managed keys and logged. Also SOC 2 controls require us to see all access events.
[01:10] Ari: To add, our firewall vendor is EdgeFort, we've got a set of 120 egress rules today. Anything that suggests opening broad outbound for model pulls is a non-starter.
[01:35] Priya: Understood. For Redwood Private we have two deployment options: VPC-hosted private control plane with customer-managed networking, or full on-prem container appliance. In VPC mode we can route all model-serving traffic through an egress NAT gateway you control, or optionally through a dedicated egress proxy we supply that supports mutual TLS.
[01:58] Samir: Quick Q — does the egress proxy support allow-listing by SNI and certificate fingerprint? We can't have DNS-based only allow lists.
[02:18] Priya: Yes we support SNI + cert pinning. We also support static IP ranges for outbound so you can create firewall allow rules. However, if you want no internet at all we recommend the on-prem appliance.
[02:40] Dr. Lena: Our compliance team will push for on-prem for PHI-adjacent workloads. But we'd like to see the VPC approach for less sensitive pipelines. So we need clear separation and RBAC to ensure dev teams can't accidentally route PII to hosted models.
[03:05] Jordan: Can we walk through a sample network flow? Priya, do you have the whiteboard?
[03:22] Priya: Sure, sketching: client request -> internal API gateway -> service account auth -> Redwood ingress endpoint (mutual TLS) -> model runner in dedicated pool -> response back. Important piece: KV cache and prefix cache stored encrypted; we offer both server-managed and customer-managed KMS.
[03:48] Ari: When you say customer-managed KMS, do you integrate with AWS KMS and on-prem HSMs? We need to ensure key material never leaves our HSM.
[04:06] Priya: We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and can integrate with partner HSMs using an agent for key wrapping. For on-prem we can do a hybrid where key ops are proxied to your HSM — there are extra latencies but keys never leave.
[04:28] Samir: Latency question — if we proxy to on-prem HSM for every token encryption call, that will add ~20-60ms per call. Does Redwood support local key caches with short TTL to reduce chattiness?
[04:48] Priya: Yes we support ephemeral wrapped keys (session keys) with adjustable TTLs. We'll also provide guidance on rotation and revoke workflows.
[05:10] Dr. Lena: Audit logs — we need immutable logs for all read/write ops on model artifacts and KMS ops. Retention 7 years, and ship to our SIEM (Splunk). Can Redwood forward audit logs in near real-time?
[05:33] Jordan: Yes, we can push log streams to your syslog/S3/Splunk HEC endpoint. There's an integration playbook we'll share. Logs can be PII-scrubbed or full fidelity depending on your retention and redaction policies.
[05:55] Ari: For egress control, can Redwood provide a hardened egress gateway that enforces protocol-level inspection and TLS termination so we can block suspicious payloads?
[06:16] Priya: Our egress gateway supports deep packet inspection via integrated filters and can terminate TLS. Note DPI may require additional legal review per locale. For strict environments we recommend no egress or allow-list IP + SNI + cert pinning.
[06:40] Samir: What about split-horizon DNS? We use different DNS answers internally vs externally to prevent accidental egress to public addresses.
[06:55] Priya: We support private endpoints and can publish private DNS records into your VPC via conditional forwarders.
[07:12] Dr. Lena: SSO mapping — we use Okta. Need to ensure service accounts are separate from user accounts, and we must limit who can create model deployments.
[07:30] Priya: We recommend RBAC tiers: Admin, DevOps, App-Service, Read-Only. SAML groups can map to these roles; we'll provide a sample mapping. Also support for SCIM provisioning.
[07:50] Jordan: I'll note action: Redwood to produce a sample SAML + SCIM mapping doc.
[08:05] Ari: Encryption in transit — we require mutual TLS with client certs for all model-serving endpoints. Does Redwood rotate server certs automatically?
[08:20] Priya: Yes server cert rotation is automated. Client cert management can be integrated with your PKI, or we can accept certs you upload.
[08:35] Dr. Lena: For SOC 2 evidence, we'll need control narratives, test results, and service org auditor attestations. Do you have a standard package?
[08:50] Jordan: Yes we'll send our SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate, along with control narratives and our audit log retention policy. Expect in the shared drive link I'll send after call.
[09:08] Samir: Edge case: If Dedicated GPU pool is exhausted and Redwood falls back to hosted (cheaper shared) model variant, how is data segregation maintained?
[09:30] Priya: We have routing policies. For customers who require strict isolation we can prevent fallback entirely. For others we can fallback only to pinned model variants that run in EU-only hosts and still honor KMS and logging constraints. We'll show config snippets.
[09:54] Dr. Lena: Good. Also we need the ability to run periodic pen tests and have Redwood coordinate with our security team for a schedule.
[10:10] Priya: Absolutely. We run internal scans and welcome customer-sponsored pen tests under an NDA — we'll provide contact and a test plan template.
[10:28] Jordan: Let's talk emergency revocation — say a key is compromised, how fast can we revoke and what are the impacts?
[10:42] Priya: Revoke is immediate at the KMS-level. We also support rolling key rotation across ephemeral caches and can invalidate session keys. Actual in-flight requests may succeed if session keys are valid until expiry; we can shorten TTL during an incident.
[11:05] Ari: On firewalling, we need a sample iptables/EdgeFort rule set and suggested IDS signatures to block exfil patterns.
[11:22] Priya: We'll produce a rule template. Note: IDS signatures are vendor-specific but we can propose generic patterns (large outbound bursts, high-entropy payloads).
[11:40] Speaker 1: (unclear) can you repeat the certificate pinning detail?
[11:47] Priya: Sure — cert pinning includes recording server certificate fingerprints at deployment; our egress proxy validates those. We'll include instructions for automating fingerprint updates when rotating certs.
[12:05] Dr. Lena: About data residency — we must ensure backups and snapshots remain in EEA. Does Redwood allow you to pin snapshot regions?
[12:20] Priya: Yes region pinning is supported, both for model artifacts and KV cache snapshots. For Dedicated we can provision local storage in the region you specify.
[12:36] Samir: Logging schema question — can Redwood include request_id, user_id, model_version, and masked prompt hash in logs so we can trace without exposing full prompt?
[12:52] Priya: Yes that's the recommended pattern — include identifiers and a reversible or one-way hash depending on audit needs. We'll share the schema.
[13:10] Dr. Lena: Any constraints around export controls or third-party models? We need to ensure exported models don't contain restricted tech.
[13:28] Jordan: We maintain a model catalog with verified sources and can block certain model variants per account. We'll add export-control notes to the policy doc.
[13:45] Ari: Operational question — if we run on-prem appliance, what's the uplift for ops headcount? How much runbook do you hand over?
[13:58] Priya: For on-prem we provide an operator playbook, monitoring dashboards, and runbook templates. Typical customer requires 1 FTE part-time during ramp, then <0.5 FTE ongoing if using our managed update pipeline.
[14:15] Samir: Can we map alerting into our PagerDuty with specific runbooks per alert type?
[14:26] Priya: Yes. We'll provide recommended thresholds and pre-built PagerDuty integrations.
[14:40] Dr. Lena: One more on compliance — we need to see your vulnerability disclosure program and timeline for critical CVEs.
[14:52] Jordan: We'll attach our VDP and typical SLA to patch production critical issues (usually 72 hours for critical, varies by risk).
[15:05] Priya: Wrapping up, I'll summarize the hard requirements we heard: no default public egress for PHI, KMS with HSM integration for sensitive keys, audit log forwarding to Splunk, RBAC via Okta SAML mapping, and region pinning for snapshots.
[15:25] Ari: That aligns with internal ask. Next practical step: we'll send you the sanitized ACL export and a network diagram of our current VPCs.
[15:38] Jordan: Great. We'll follow up with SOC 2 package and the network rule template. Also propose a short pilot: spin up a Dedicated node in EU with customer-managed KMS and run a three-day workload to measure latency and egress controls.
[15:58] Dr. Lena: Sounds good. Please include expected cost delta for KMS-on-prem vs server-managed.
[16:10] Priya: We'll include a cost delta sheet. Also note small caveat: HSM proxied mode may add 20-60ms so we'll show mitigation strategies (session keys, caching).
[16:30] Jordan: Any other open questions?
[16:35] Maya (Compliance): One ask: can Redwood redact PII at ingestion before logs land in our SIEM? We want both full-fidelity in an encrypted archive and PII-reduced stream for Splunk.
[16:50] Priya: Yes we support dual-stream: encrypted archive (S3 with customer-managed keys) plus redacted stream to your SIEM. We'll document fields and redaction rules.
[17:05] Samir: For the pilot we'll need a small playbook of sample prompts and test vectors to validate redaction works.
[17:18] Priya: We'll provide a standard prompt set and test harness.
[17:30] Jordan: Ok we'll capture next steps and get the artifacts out. Thanks everyone.

Recap / Action items (spoken):
- Redwood: SOC 2 + ISO docs, RBAC mapping sample, network/firewall templates, cost delta sheet for KMS modes, pilot plan (Jordan/Priya)
- Novus: sanitized firewall rules + VPC diagram, confirm data residency constraints, schedule pilot window (Ari/Samir)
